## Research Question

Describe your research question here. Include why this question might be of interest. 

Does neighbourhood drive up sale prices in the central area of Ames, Iowa or are other factors more influential in dtermining sale price?
sub questions: 1) is the relationship between quality / condition and price negligible or significant?
2) does the period of remodelling and orginal construction heave great significance on sale price?
3) the role of structural characteristics in determining sale price in Iowa (ie house style - stories, area etc.)

House prices data is datatset which includes prices of houses sold in Iowa between 2006 and 2010, and their various features, such as basement quality,  and overall condition, along with structural characteristics such as stories and overall quality, across different residential areas. 




## Findings

Inital findings from graph 1) Price of houses by era BUILT = median/ avg of victorian & gilded age = lowest (marginally in comparison to interwar and post war but more prominently in comparison to 20th century & modern), Victorian & gilded age have more significant extreme price variety, while post war has least extreme price variety, 20th century & modern has overall highest average, avg across all eras is less than/ equal to $200,000, 20th century & modern has no extremes, 2) Prices of houses by era REMODELLED = inc relationship as median price increases as move closer to recent remodelling,  both 1980s&1990s and 2000s have no lower extremes, but high ones (1980s and 1990s has highest extreme), 3) House prices by area = majority lie above line of best fit, houses with fewer stories but higher sq footage are one of the groups under the line of best fit, while houses with fewer stories and less sq footage also remain under the line but closer to origin = P and area relationship between these specific = P remains relatively unresponsive to higher sq footage when the house has genereally fewer stories, above best fit lies houses with more stories but some share the saem sq footage as those under with a lower sale price, again reinforcing the idea that area isnt the strongest determinant here, instead the syle suggests the sale price, there is a result that lies way above and off the line, but cluster remains around the line 4) is similar just curved line, 5) Prices of houses by neighbourhood = highest avg belongs to crawford, lowest belongs to old town, edwards & idotrr & swissu & brookside lie in a close range to each other (roughly between $100,000 and $150,000), Old town has highest extreme and lowest extreme

The visualisation comparing size of houses with the Neighborhood confirms that size is not necessarily the most influential factor and that neighbourhood is a fairly substantial factor. Since Crawford and college creek have higher house prices independent of area when compoared to other nighbourhoods in the central area such as Edwards or Berkside.
